## Declarations and implementations

```plato

// The closest point on a 3D surface to a query point. IFace is the triangle
// holding the closest point (-1 when the target is not a mesh); Barycentric
// locates it within that triangle.
type ClosestPointResult3D
    implements IValue
{
    Position: Point3D;
    Distance: Number;
    Face: FaceIndex;
    Barycentric: BarycentricCoordinate;
}

// The closest pair between two indexed sets
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closest_pair_of_points_problem): IndexA into
// the first set, IndexB into the second, and the separating distance (0 when
// touching or overlapping).
type ClosestPairResult
    implements IValue
{
    IndexA: ItemIndex;
    IndexB: ItemIndex;
    Distance: Number;
}

//==
// # Ray and sweep queries
//
// Raycast and sphere-sweep requests and their hit records, kept as plain data so
// they can be batched, serialized, and replayed. Distances are world-space and
// non-negative; a MaxDistance that is zero or negative means "unbounded";
// FilterMask is a category bitmask combined with a candidate's category bits by
// bitwise AND (non-zero passes), and -1 (all bits set) accepts everything.

// A bounded, filtered 2D raycast request
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_casting).
type RayQuery2D
    implements IValue
{
    Ray: Ray2D;
    MaxDistance: Number;
    FilterMask: Integer;
}

// A bounded, filtered 3D raycast request.
type RayQuery3D
    implements IValue
{
    Ray: Ray3D;
    MaxDistance: Number;
    FilterMask: Integer;
}

// A sphere-sweep (thick ray) request: a sphere of the given radius travels
// along the ray until it first touches something.
type SweepQuery3D
    implements IValue
{
    Ray: Ray3D;
    Radius: Number;
    MaxDistance: Number;
    FilterMask: Integer;
}

// The result of a 2D raycast. When Hit is false the remaining fields are
// meaningless. Distance is measured from the ray origin along its
// direction; Normal points against the ray (out of the struck primitive);
// PrimitiveIndex identifies the struck primitive in the caller's list,
// -1 when inapplicable.
type RayHit2D
    implements IValue
{
    Hit: Boolean;
    Distance: Number;
    Position: Point2D;
    Normal: Direction2D;
    PrimitiveIndex: ItemIndex;
}

// The result of a 3D raycast against triangulated geometry. When Hit is false
// the remaining fields are meaningless. IFace is the struck triangle (-1 when
// the target is not a mesh); Barycentric locates the hit within that triangle
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barycentric_coordinate_system); Uv is the
// interpolated surface parameter at the hit, (0, 0) when the target carries no
// UVs.
type RayHit3D
    implements IValue
{
    Hit: Boolean;
    Distance: Number;
    Position: Point3D;
    Normal: Direction3D;
    Face: FaceIndex;
    Barycentric: BarycentricCoordinate;
    Uv: UvCoordinate;
}

//==
// # Bounding volume hierarchies and region trees
//
// Pure-data hierarchical indexes over collections of primitives, plus the node
// index shared by every spatial structure in this vocabulary. Every structure
// follows the same flat-array conventions:
//
// - Nodes live in one array; a node refers to other nodes by SpatialNodeIndex
//   position in that array, with -1 meaning "no child". Node 0 is the root.
// - A structure never stores primitives; it stores a permutation array of
//   primitive indices (Array<ItemIndex>) into the caller's primitive list.
//   Leaves reference half-open IntegerInterval ranges of that permutation.
// - An empty range (Start equals End) means "no items".

// A zero-based index of a node within a spatial structure's flat node array.
// -1 means "no child" / "leaf".
type SpatialNodeIndex
    implements IValue, IHashable, IComparable, IIndex
{
    Value: Integer;
}

//==
// ## Bounding volume hierarchies

// One node of a 2D bounding volume hierarchy. Internal nodes carry child
// node indices and an empty Primitives range; leaves carry LeftChild and
// RightChild of -1 and a non-empty half-open range into the owning
// hierarchy's PrimitiveIndices.
type BvhNode2D
    implements IValue
{
    Bounds: Bounds2D;
    LeftChild: SpatialNodeIndex;
    RightChild: SpatialNodeIndex;
    Primitives: IntegerInterval;
}

// A binary bounding volume hierarchy
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bounding_volume_hierarchy) over 2D
// primitives. Node 0 is the root; PrimitiveIndices is the leaf-order
// permutation of the caller's primitive list. No builder yet: instances come
// from a host, until BuildBvh (spatial-structures.library.plato) gains a 2D
// twin — see tracker/decisions/2026-08-04-spatial-structure-construction-in-plato.md.
type Bvh2D
    implements IValue, ISpatialIndex2D
{
    Nodes: Array<BvhNode2D>;
    PrimitiveIndices: Array<ItemIndex>;
}

// One node of a 3D bounding volume hierarchy. Same encoding as BvhNode2D
// with 3D bounds.
type BvhNode3D
    implements IValue
{
    Bounds: Bounds3D;
    LeftChild: SpatialNodeIndex;
    RightChild: SpatialNodeIndex;
    Primitives: IntegerInterval;
}
```
